title: A generic-point flat basis becomes universally injective over a base open
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], with geometrically integral fibres, meaning that each $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ remains a nonzero domain under every field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak s)$. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be prime and let $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pB$ be prime with inverse image $\mathfrak p$. Let $E$ be a finitely presented $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], let $r\geq0$, and fix a $B$-linear map $\alpha:B^{\oplus r}\to E$ whose tensor product with $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is an isomorphism. Assume only that $E_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Then there is $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $\alpha_f:B_f^{\oplus r}\to E_f$ is universally injective over $R_f$: for every $R_f$-module $L$, $L\otimes_{R_f}\alpha_f$ is injective. Subscripts $f$ and prime ideals denote module or ring localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]; tensor products and residue fields are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and [def-weil-residue-field]. Global $R$-flatness of $E$ is not assumed.

source.place: Tag 05IA (lemma-induction-step-fp), implication (1) to the universal-injectivity part of (2), applied at q=pB.

proof.text: Put $A=R_{\mathfrak p}$, $C=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B$, $M=(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}E$, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA$. The prime $\mathfrak q$ becomes $\xi=\mathfrak mC$; the hypothesis $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$ identifies $C_\xi=B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $M_\xi=E_{\mathfrak q}$ by the fraction maps. Localization of a finite algebra presentation and a finite module presentation gives finite presentations of $C/A$ and $M/C$; exactness is [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Localizing the $R$-flat module $B$ preserves $R$-flatness by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness]; [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] then gives $A$-flatness of $C$. Fibres of $C/A$ are the original fibres over primes contained in $\mathfrak p$, with the same residue fields, so remain geometrically integral. The given residue-field isomorphism is unchanged. Apply [lem-trf-local-generic-basis-universal-injective] to $A\to C$, $M$, and the specified map $\alpha_A$, with its point $\xi$. Its flatness hypothesis is exactly $E_{\mathfrak q}$ flat over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. It gives universal injectivity of $\alpha_A$.

source.place: Tag 05IA (lemma-induction-step-fp), proof of (1) implies (2), universal-injectivity assertion.

proof.text: Taking the testing module $A$ shows $\alpha_A$ is injective. Localizing at $\xi$ preserves injectivity by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so $\alpha_{\mathfrak q}$ is injective. The images of its $r$ standard vectors span $E_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{B_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ by hypothesis. The module $E_{\mathfrak q}$ is finite, since its finite presentation localizes. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] these vectors generate $E_{\mathfrak q}$, so $\alpha_{\mathfrak q}$ is also surjective, hence an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization] the assumed $R_{\mathfrak p}$-flatness of $E_{\mathfrak q}$ is equivalent to $R$-flatness.

source.place: Tag 05IA (lemma-induction-step-fp), proof of (1) implies (2), universal-injectivity assertion.

proof.text: Let $U_1=\{t\in\operatorname{Spec}B:E_t\text{ is }R\text{-flat}\}$ and $U_2=\{t\in\operatorname{Spec}B:\alpha_t\text{ is an isomorphism}\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-openness-of-flatness], $U_1$ is open: $B/R$ and $E/B$ have the required finite presentations. To see $U_2$ is open, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-to-finitely-presented-map-iso-at-prime-spreads] at each of its points, with finite source $B^{\oplus r}$ and finitely presented target $E$. It supplies $g\notin t$ with $\alpha_g$ bijective, hence $D(g)\subset U_2$ by localization; these neighbourhoods cover $U_2$. Step 2 gives $\mathfrak q\in U_1\cap U_2$. The spectral map $\Phi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-finite-presentation-open]. Thus $V=\Phi(U_1\cap U_2)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$. Choose $f\notin\mathfrak p$ with $D(f)\subset V$, using the standard-open basis of the Zariski topology.

source.place: Tag 05IA (lemma-induction-step-fp), proof of (1) implies (2), universal-injectivity assertion.

proof.text: For each $\mathfrak s\in D(f)$ choose $t\in U_1\cap U_2$ over $\mathfrak s$. The nonzero domain $F_{\mathfrak s}=B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak s)$ has zero prime, whose inverse image $\zeta_{\mathfrak s}\subset B$ is contained in $t$: every prime of the fibre contains its zero prime. Consequently $\zeta_{\mathfrak s}$ is a generalization of $t$. Opens are stable under generalization, since a standard open $D(g)$ containing $t$ also contains every subprime of $t$. Hence $\zeta_{\mathfrak s}\in U_1\cap U_2$. In particular $E_{\zeta_{\mathfrak s}}$ is $R$-flat and $\alpha_{\zeta_{\mathfrak s}}$ is an isomorphism. It is flat over $R_{\mathfrak s}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], because this stalk has an $R_{\mathfrak s}$-module structure. Tensoring an isomorphism with $\kappa(\zeta_{\mathfrak s})$ remains an isomorphism: tensor its inverse to obtain the inverse. These are precisely the flatness and residue-basis hypotheses at every fibre generic point over $D(f)$.

source.place: Tag 05IA (lemma-induction-step-fp), proof of (1) implies (2), universal-injectivity assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-free-subtraction-flatness] to $R_f\to B_f$, the finite $B_f$-module $E_f$, and the specified $\alpha_f$. As in step 1, localization of the finite presentations, preservation of flatness by [lem-pc-affine-flat-module-localization-preserves-flatness] and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], and the unchanged residue fields show that this is a flat finitely presented algebra with geometrically integral fibres. Every prime of $R_f$ corresponds to a unique $\mathfrak s\in D(f)$, and its fibre generic point corresponds to $\zeta_{\mathfrak s}$. The localization identifications send $(E_f)_{\zeta_{\mathfrak s}B_f}$ to $E_{\zeta_{\mathfrak s}}$ and the residue map to that of step 4. All hypotheses of the cited node therefore hold. Its first conclusion says that $L\otimes_{R_f}\alpha_f$ is injective for every $R_f$-module $L$, as required. Only flatness at the original $\mathfrak q$ and on the explicitly constructed open $U_1$ has been used.

Step 1: localizing at p, 00CS and 00HT carry finite presentation and flatness over, and all hypotheses of the local 05I3 node hold at xi=pB_p, so alpha_A is universally injective. Step 2: alpha_q is injective by localization and surjective by the Nakayama node, hence an isomorphism. Step 4 (elementary): the fibre generic point zeta_s is a generalization of t, so it lies in U_1 and U_2.
